35288282.clinical_problem: Recovering missing or poor-quality T2-weighted anatomical MRI in neonates so that downstream image processing (e.g., resting-state fMRI pipelines) is not lost
35288282.model_description: Two methods, a deep-learning image synthesis model and a nonlinear multi-atlas registration method, that generate pseudo-T2-weighted images from other neonatal MRI data to substitute for missing or unusable T2w scans.
35288282.dataset_size: two independent neonatal cohorts (exact n not stated)
35288282.study_design: retrospective method development and evaluation across two independent neonatal cohorts

35349359.model_family: Random Forest (best of several classical classifiers: KNN, decision tree, SVM, Naive Bayes, multiclassifier)
35349359.clinical_problem: Classifying umbilical cord coiling pattern from prenatal Doppler ultrasound
35349359.patient_population: pregnant women undergoing umbilical cord Doppler ultrasound (exact n not stated)
35349359.model_description: Texture features and a newly proposed umbilical coiling index extracted from 2-D Doppler ultrasound images are used with SMOTE oversampling and classical machine-learning classifiers to classify umbilical cord type.
35349359.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with imbalanced-data handling (SMOTE)

35383946.clinical_problem: Reducing radiation dose during pediatric cardiac catheterization by predicting X-ray angiography frames instead of acquiring every frame
35383946.patient_population: pediatric cardiac intervention patients; validated on 56 simulated and 52 patients' X-ray angiography sequences
35383946.model_description: A model-free motion estimation network (LSTM) paired with a CNN content predictor estimates coronary artery motion and predicts future X-ray angiography frames, reducing the number of pulses required while preserving image quality.
35383946.dataset_size: 56 simulated and 52 patients' X-ray angiography sequences
35383946.headline_result: structural similarity index 97% (simulated), 82% (patient) data; pulse count reduced by up to 3 frames, about 30% dose reduction per second

35425784.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring fetal head circumference from prenatal ultrasound to monitor fetal growth
35425784.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound (HC18 public dataset)
35425784.model_description: A one-stage, end-to-end rotating elliptic object detector combining a CNN (ResDCN) with a transformer detects the fetal skull outline in 2-D ultrasound and computes head circumference without post-processing.
35425784.dataset_size: HC18 public dataset (exact n not stated)
35425784.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation on the public HC18 benchmark

35431841.clinical_problem: Automatically identifying the type of artifact present in diffusion MRI scans to flag poor-quality scans before further analysis
35431841.patient_population: children and adolescents from the ABCD and Healthy Brain Network cohorts
35431841.model_description: A two-step 3D residual squeeze-and-excitation CNN predicts the artifact type present in sub-volumes of a diffusion MRI scan, then a voting step outputs the overall artifact class for the whole volume.
35431841.dataset_size: 2,494 poor-quality dMRI volumes (ABCD) and 4,226 (Healthy Brain Network)
35431841.headline_result: average accuracy 96.61% (ABCD) and 97.52% (Healthy Brain Network) test sets
35431841.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation across two independent large-scale pediatric MRI cohorts

35537665.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring liver volume from MRI in adolescents with obesity
35537665.model_description: 3D U-Net convolutional neural networks trained on different MRI sequence combinations (Dixon water, fat, T2* images, and T2-weighted scout images) automatically segment the liver and compute liver volume.
35537665.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.94, normalized RMSE 4.2% (best model, water+fat images)
35537665.study_design: retrospective model development with internal validation against manual segmentation

35572069.clinical_problem: Automatically flagging poor-quality infant cortical surface reconstructions from brain MRI caused by low tissue contrast or motion
35572069.model_description: A spherical transformer applied to the spherical mapping of infant cortical surface meshes automatically assesses reconstruction quality, extending spherical CNN methods with transformer-based contextual feature learning.

35585465.clinical_problem: Distinguishing the causative organism (viral, bacterial, or mycoplasma) of community-acquired pneumonia in children from chest radiographs
35585465.model_description: A context-fusion CNN combines full-lung and local pneumonia-lesion image features from chest radiographs, with an optional logistic-regression combination with CRP and white blood cell count, to classify pneumonia etiology.
35585465.dataset_size: 1,769 pediatric pneumonia cases (487 viral, 496 bacterial, 786 mycoplasma)
35585465.study_design: retrospective model development with internal 7:1:2 train/validation/test split

35655747.clinical_problem: Distinguishing children and young adults with post-traumatic headache after concussion from healthy controls using combined behavioral and brain imaging data
35655747.patient_population: pediatric and young adult subjects with post-traumatic headache and healthy controls (exact n not stated)
35655747.model_description: Machine-learning classifiers combine self-report questionnaire data (concussion symptoms, mental health, pain experience) with structural brain MRI features from cortical and subcortical regions to classify post-traumatic headache versus healthy controls.
35655747.study_design: retrospective case-control study with machine-learning classification

35783351.clinical_problem: Automatically detecting and grading the severity of imaging artifacts (motion, chemical shift, radiofrequency) in fetal MRI for quality assurance
35783351.patient_population: fetal MRI scans (exact n not stated)
35783351.model_description: A CNN ensemble (RISE-Net) first classifies the artifact type present in 3D fetal MRI, then a second CNN regresses the severity of the detected artifact.
35783351.headline_result: classification accuracy 90.34%, F1 score 90.39%; severity regression MSE 0.083
35783351.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation, benchmarked against other CNN architectures

35917308.model_family: 3D U-Net (with ResNet/SENet enhancements) plus neural-network regression
35917308.clinical_problem: Predicting a child's fluid intelligence score from structural brain MRI
35917308.patient_population: children from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Neurocognitive Prediction Challenge dataset
35917308.model_description: A two-step deep-learning pipeline first segments brain regions of interest using an enhanced 3D U-Net, then trains a neural-network regression model on those regions to predict a fluid intelligence score from T1-weighted MRI.
35917308.dataset_size: ABCD Neurocognitive Prediction Challenge dataset (exact n not stated)
35917308.headline_result: segmentation Dice coefficient 0.8920; fluid intelligence prediction mean squared error 82.56 on the test set
35917308.study_design: retrospective algorithm development for the ABCD Neurocognitive Prediction Challenge

36061501.model_family: Gradient Boosting (best of SVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting)
36061501.clinical_problem: Classifying children with ADHD versus typically developing children using brain network connectivity measures from resting-state fMRI
36061501.patient_population: 56 drug-naive children with ADHD and 56 age-matched typically developing controls
36061501.model_description: Graph-theoretical network measures extracted from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity are reduced with recursive feature elimination and used to train SVM, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting classifiers to distinguish ADHD from typically developing children.
36061501.dataset_size: 56 ADHD children and 56 typically developing controls (ADHD-200 Peking dataset)
36061501.study_design: retrospective case-control classification study using the public ADHD-200 dataset

36082304.model_family: logistic regression and SVM (best of six classical classifiers)
36082304.clinical_problem: Classifying pediatric bipolar disorder type I from healthy controls using structural brain MRI measures
36082304.patient_population: 33 pediatric bipolar disorder type I patients and 19 age/sex-matched healthy controls
36082304.model_description: Brain cortical thickness and subcortical volume features from structural MRI are reduced via Lasso or f_classif feature selection and used to train six classical machine-learning classifiers (logistic regression, SVM, random forest, naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbor, AdaBoost) to distinguish pediatric bipolar disorder from healthy controls.
36082304.dataset_size: 33 pediatric bipolar disorder type I patients and 19 healthy controls

36093771.exclusion_reason: Classifies adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity from lumbosacral joint efforts during gait (biomechanical data), explicitly proposed as a radiation-free alternative to radiography; no radiologic imaging is used as model input.

36248649.body_region: brain (gray matter: occipito-temporal cortex, insular, inferior frontal, supramarginal gyri)
36248649.clinical_problem: Predicting a child's future reading/literacy ability two years later from preliterate brain structure and cognitive-linguistic skills
36248649.patient_population: 42 native German-speaking children scanned at the end of kindergarten
36248649.model_description: A leave-one-out cross-validated machine-learning regression model uses gray matter morphology features from T1-weighted MRI plus preliterate cognitive-linguistic test scores to predict literacy skills measured two years later.
36248649.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort with machine-learning prediction analysis

36271054.body_region: vascular malformations (extremity/soft tissue, region not further specified)
36271054.clinical_problem: Differentiating fibro-adipose vascular anomaly from common venous malformation on MRI to guide diagnosis and management
36271054.patient_population: 178 children, adolescents and young adults with vascular malformations (41 fibro-adipose vascular anomaly, 137 venous malformation)
36271054.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from T1-weighted and fat-saturated T2-weighted MRI, selected via LASSO or Boruta methods, are used to train weighted logistic regression models that classify vascular malformations as fibro-adipose vascular anomaly versus common venous malformation.
36271054.dataset_size: 178 patients (41 fibro-adipose vascular anomaly, 137 venous malformation)
36271054.headline_result: AUC 97% (sensitivity 94-95%, specificity 87-89%) for the best multi-sequence models
36271054.study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development with repeated 10-fold cross-validation

36312010.clinical_problem: Differentiating preterm from term infant brains and identifying the structural/functional biomarkers of prematurity
36312010.patient_population: infants from the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) dataset
36312010.model_description: A graph neural network built on DICCCOL cortical landmarks combines resting-state functional MRI activity and structural fiber connectivity as graph node and edge features, using self-attention graph pooling to classify preterm versus term infant brains and identify discriminative biomarkers.
36312010.dataset_size: developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) dataset (exact n not stated)
36312010.study_design: retrospective algorithm development on the public dHCP dataset

36505382.exclusion_reason: Narrative review of myocardial strain imaging in Duchenne muscular dystrophy; deep learning for automated strain assessment is mentioned only briefly as a future/emerging technique, not the focus of the review.

36523363.exclusion_reason: Diagnostic model based on phonocardiogram (heart sound audio recordings), not radiologic imaging; the 'optical coherence tomography network' is only the name of the classifier architecture, not an imaging modality used.

36563062.clinical_problem: Predicting an infant's brain functional connectivity at a target age from earlier resting-state fMRI, to fill gaps in longitudinal infant brain development studies caused by missing scans
36563062.model_description: A conditional intensive triplet auto-encoder network disentangles age-related and identity-related information from an infant's resting-state functional connectivity to predict that infant's functional connectivity at any specified target age.

36685346.exclusion_reason: Review of retinal/fundus imaging, OCT, and telemedicine for retinopathy of prematurity; non-radiologic (ophthalmic) imaging.

36699518.clinical_problem: Building a predictive neurotypicality score from brain functional connectivity to help identify atypical neurodevelopment in children and adolescents
36699518.patient_population: 377 neurotypical and 126 atypical children and adolescents from a community-based cohort
36699518.model_description: An ensemble of GAN discriminators trained on neurotypical resting-state fMRI functional connectivity patterns produces a predictive neurotypicality score three years after scanning, with LIME used to identify explanatory functional hubs.
36699518.study_design: prospective community-based cohort with retrospective GAN-based modeling

36798853.model_family: CNN (custom architecture combining MRI volumes, radiomics, and feature maps)
36798853.clinical_problem: Predicting before delivery whether placenta accreta spectrum will be severe enough to require emergency hysterectomy
36798853.patient_population: 241 pregnant patients with placenta accreta spectrum
36798853.model_description: A convolutional network architecture (CascadeNet) combines MRI volumes, radiomic features, and custom feature maps to predict whether placenta accreta spectrum will require hysterectomy after fetal delivery.
36798853.study_design: retrospective model development with internal train/validation/test split

36962760.exclusion_reason: Gestational age estimation from newborn screening metabolites (blood test panel); laboratory-based model, not radiologic imaging.

39911317.model_family: CNN (U-Net-like architecture with a context encoding module)
39911317.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting cranial bones and localizing craniofacial landmarks from CT or MR images to support craniofacial analysis
39911317.patient_population: 274 pediatric subjects with diverse craniofacial conditions
39911317.model_description: A U-Net-like network with a novel context encoding module jointly performs single-stage cranial bone labeling (segmentation) and craniofacial landmark localization from CT (or MR) images, with an auxiliary task modeling the spatial configuration between landmarks.
39911317.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation on a pediatric craniofacial CT dataset

33616744.exclusion_reason: Adult study (127 young women) using conventional regression analysis relating cortical thickness to heart-rate variability; no AI/ML method, not pediatric.

33968311.exclusion_reason: General review of COVID-19 clinical/radiological discrepancies across all ages; AI-based CXR algorithms and pediatric MRI safety are each mentioned only in passing, not the focus.

34101118.model_family: support vector machine (best of nine machine-learning models tested; radiomics-based)
34101118.clinical_problem: Predicting the causative bacterial class (Gram-positive, Gram-negative, or atypical) of pediatric bacterial pneumonia from low-dose chest CT to guide empirical antibiotic therapy
34101118.patient_population: 389 children with pathogen-confirmed bacterial pneumonia (122 Gram-positive, 159 Gram-negative, 108 atypical)
34101118.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from low-dose chest CT images are used to build three machine-learning submodels (Gram-positive, Gram-negative, atypical) that are integrated into a support-vector-machine-based multi-class classifier predicting the causative bacterial class of pneumonia.
34101118.dataset_size: 389 children (122 Gram-positive, 159 Gram-negative, 108 atypical bacterial pneumonia)
34101118.study_design: retrospective radiomics model development with internal train/test split

34101855.clinical_problem: Detecting small lumbar stress lesions on 99mTc-MDP SPECT bone scans in pediatric patients with low back pain, compared with physician performance
34101855.patient_population: 65 lesion-absent pediatric SPECT studies with simulated inserted lesions; test set also reviewed by 5 physicians
34101855.model_description: A deep CNN trained on 2.5D views extracted from simulated lesion-present and lesion-absent 99mTc-MDP SPECT images is applied in a sliding-window fashion to generate a 3D heatmap of lesion probability at each lumbar location, compared against physician localization performance in an LROC study.
34101855.dataset_size: 65 lesion-absent pediatric SPECT studies (artificial lesions inserted for evaluation)
34101855.headline_result: AUC-LROC 0.830 (deep learning) vs 0.785 (average of five physicians)
34101855.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with cross-validation and a physician reader-comparison (LROC) study

34130195.exclusion_reason: Feasibility study of CNNs for detecting malformations of cortical development on MRI; the abstract does not state a pediatric population or age range.

34303948.exclusion_reason: Adult population (346 male inpatient cocaine users) studying retrospectively recalled childhood trauma via questionnaires and machine learning; no imaging, not pediatric radiology.

34605964.model_family: deep learning CT reconstruction (six manufacturer-standard DLR algorithms)
34605964.clinical_problem: Comparing deep-learning CT image reconstruction to standard iterative reconstruction for detecting urinary tract stones in children and young adults on unenhanced CT
34605964.patient_population: 14 patients (mean age 17.3 ± 3.4 years, 5 males, 9 females), reconstructed into 84 total exams
34605964.model_description: Six manufacturer-standard deep-learning CT reconstruction algorithms were applied to clinically acquired unenhanced abdomen/pelvis CT scans, and three blinded radiologists identified and measured urinary tract stones on the reconstructed images, compared against standard iterative reconstruction as a reference.
34605964.dataset_size: 14 patients (84 total reconstructed exams across 6 DLR algorithms)
34605964.headline_result: interobserver agreement kappa 0.71-1 for calculus presence; ICC 0.78-0.96 for calculus count; ICC 0.51-0.97 for calculus size, depending on algorithm and reviewer
34605964.study_design: retrospective post-hoc reconstruction study with blinded reader comparison to a reference standard

34647145.exclusion_reason: Adult population (214 patients with chronic liver disease/cirrhosis); predictive model uses clinical laboratory values (bilirubin, albumin, MELD-Na, Child-Pugh score), not radiologic image features, and no pediatric population stated.

34712295.exclusion_reason: Title references an SVM algorithm, but the abstract describes only conventional statistical analysis (chi-square test, multivariate logistic regression) of clinical and Doppler ultrasound findings in gestational diabetes; no machine-learning methodology or results are reported.

34717846.exclusion_reason: Review of ultrashort/zero echo-time pediatric bone MR imaging technique and clinical applications (craniosynostosis, sinonasal/jaw imaging, trauma); deep learning is mentioned only in passing as one of three approaches to synthetic CT generation, not the review's focus.

34883946.model_family: CNN (residual CNN localization + boundary-preserving fully convolutional dense nets)
34883946.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting the kidney and its cortex/medulla compartments from pediatric dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI to compute markers of kidney function such as glomerular filtration rate
34883946.patient_population: 60 4D DCE-MRI volumes from pediatric patients with varying conditions affecting kidney function
34883946.model_description: A dual-stage deep-learning framework first localizes and segments each kidney using residual convolutional neural networks with spatial-temporal, boundary-preserving fully convolutional dense nets, then further segments the cortex and medulla to compute quantitative kidney-function markers from 4D DCE-MRI.
34883946.headline_result: 3.8% higher mean Dice similarity coefficient than a state-of-the-art comparison method (GrabCut + SVM)
34883946.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal evaluation on a pediatric DCE-MRI dataset

32089729.model_family: random forest classification + Gaussian mixture model (probabilistic point-cloud registration)
32089729.clinical_problem: Automatically registering 3D fetal brain ultrasound volumes affected by acoustic occlusion and noise, to monitor fetal brain growth and support brain-atlas-based segmentation
32089729.patient_population: 3D ultrasound fetal brain volumes (exact n not stated)
32089729.model_description: A supervised-learning-guided variant of the coherent point drift algorithm uses random-forest classification to weight a point cloud and assign Gaussian mixture model membership probabilities, enabling automatic registration of 3D fetal head ultrasound volumes despite occlusion artifacts and noise.
32089729.headline_result: target registration error 6.38 ± 3.24 mm; error reduction of 7.4%-60.7% versus comparison algorithms

32757145.exclusion_reason: Case series describing clinical and lung ultrasound findings in aspiration pneumonia in children; no AI/ML component.

33236529.exclusion_reason: Adult population with HBV-related liver cirrhosis and covert hepatic encephalopathy; not pediatric.

33564753.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting subcortical brain structures on infant brain MRI to study early subcortical growth patterns and related disease diagnosis
33564753.model_description: A coarse-to-fine two-stage CNN framework: a signed-distance-map-predicting U-Net (SDM-UNet) first learns spatial context (relative position and shape) from multi-modal T1w, T2w, and T1w/T2w images, then a multi-source multi-path U-Net (M2-UNet) combines this with the images to deliver refined subcortical segmentation.
33564753.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation compared with four state-of-the-art methods

33598664.model_family: semi-supervised transfer learning (deep learning, confidence-map guided)
33598664.clinical_problem: Segmenting the infant cerebellum into white matter, gray matter, and cerebrospinal fluid from MRI across ages 6-24 months despite low tissue contrast in younger infants
33598664.model_description: A semi-supervised transfer-learning framework, guided by a confidence map, propagates reliable manual cerebellum tissue labels from high-contrast 24-month-old infant MRI to progressively segment lower-contrast MRI from 18-, 12-, and 6-month-old infants.
33598664.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and comparison with state-of-the-art methods

30693378.exclusion_reason: General strategic research agenda for biomedical imaging across all of medicine; AI/machine learning is mentioned only briefly as one of several topics, not pediatric-specific.

30824170.exclusion_reason: Review of CT versus ultrasound strategy for acute abdominal pain/appendicitis across all ages; no AI/ML component.

31843832.clinical_problem: Assessing whether automated 3D ultrasound image-recognition software can reduce variability in fetal biometric measurements (head/abdominal circumference, femur length) used to estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
31843832.model_description: Automated software extracts standard reference planes from 3D ultrasound volumes of the fetal head, abdomen, and femur and computes biometric measurements automatically, to be compared with manual 2D ultrasound measurements for agreement and reproducibility.
31843832.study_design: prospective cross-sectional study protocol (trial registration NCT03812471)

31856250.exclusion_reason: The SVM classifier for identifying yawns was developed and tested on video-based behavioral coding of preterm neonates' mouth movements, not on ultrasound images; the intended future application to fetal ultrasound is discussed but not implemented or tested here.

32924031.model_family: neural network classifier (with regional-MRI-feature-substitution data augmentation)
32924031.clinical_problem: Predicting whether adolescents will transition from no/low to medium/heavy alcohol drinking based on volumetric brain MRI measurements
32924031.model_description: A data-augmentation strategy that synthetically substitutes regional brain MRI volume scores generates over one million synthetic training samples from fewer than 500 subjects, used to train a neural-network classifier predicting adolescent alcohol-use transition from volumetric MRI measurements.
32924031.dataset_size: fewer than 500 subjects, augmented to over one million synthetic samples
32924031.headline_result: 74.1% accuracy distinguishing non-drinkers from drinkers at baseline; 43.2% weighted accuracy predicting the 3-year transition (5-group classification)
32924031.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with data augmentation and 20-fold cross-validation

34278384.clinical_problem: Predicting missing longitudinal infant diffusion MRI data to fill gaps caused by subject dropout or unsuccessful scans, for studying brain microstructure development
34278384.patient_population: longitudinally acquired pediatric diffusion MRI dataset (exact n not stated)
34278384.model_description: A graph convolutional network jointly models spatial (x-space) and diffusion-angular (q-space) relationships as a graph, using a residual learning architecture to predict longitudinal changes in infant diffusion MRI data over time and fill missing timepoints.

29858509.exclusion_reason: Open-source model-based iterative CT reconstruction using coordinate-descent optimization; a classical optimization algorithm, not a machine-learning method, and the pediatric thoracic scan is only one incidental test case rather than the study's focus.

30035016.exclusion_reason: Group-comparison graph-theoretical network analysis of structural MRI in children with epilepsy; conventional statistical analysis of network metrics, not a machine-learning predictive model.

30396518.exclusion_reason: Workshop report covering placental imaging research broadly (blood flow, multimodal imaging, segmentation methods, public engagement); deep learning fetal MRI segmentation is mentioned only in passing as one of about 20 poster topics, not the report's focus.

30654905.exclusion_reason: Data mining of clinical/laboratory records (not image-based AI) to analyze the cardiac effects of childhood rheumatic fever; chest x-ray findings ('teleNormal', 'cardiomegaly') are used only as an input attribute label, not analyzed by AI.

28251155.model_family: 3D Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) with sliding-window scoring
28251155.clinical_problem: Automatically localizing the fetal brain in 3T MRI acquired as motion-affected 2D slice stacks, to enable large-scale automated fetal MRI processing and motion correction
28251155.patient_population: 104 fetal MRI scans, gestational ages 34-38 weeks
28251155.model_description: A 3D extension of the Histogram of Oriented Gradients feature descriptor scores candidate windows in a sliding-window search to automatically localize the fetal brain in motion-affected 3T MRI slice stacks, supporting downstream fetal motion correction and reconstruction.
28251155.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with leave-one-out cross-validation, compared against template matching and random forest regression

26802942.exclusion_reason: Title mentions 'youth' but the study population is described only as 'healthy subjects' with MeSH terms Adult/Young Adult; no pediatric age range is stated.

25954186.clinical_problem: Classifying adolescents with a positive versus negative familial history of substance use disorder using brain activity and connectivity during an emotional conflict task
25954186.patient_population: 11 adolescents with a positive familial history of substance use disorder and 7 with a negative familial history
25954186.model_description: Brain activation features from conflict-related functional MRI contrast images, plus Granger causality connectivity indices among brain regions, are used to train a support vector machine classifying adolescents by familial history of substance use disorder.
25954186.headline_result: classification accuracy up to 97.28% (leave-one-out cross-validation, combined activity and connectivity features)
25954186.study_design: retrospective case-control classification study with leave-one-out cross-validation

21097097.model_family: Hopfield Neural Network (hybrid with Bayesian classifier)
21097097.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting the neonatal skull on MRI to support source localization of EEG/MEG signals
21097097.model_description: A hybrid algorithm combining a Bayesian classifying framework with a Hopfield Neural Network, using locally adaptive statistical parameters to handle non-homogeneous skull intensities, segments the skull on high-resolution T1-weighted neonatal MRI.

19546330.clinical_problem: Assessing the feasibility of automated 3D ultrasound software for extended basic fetal cardiac screening in routine prenatal ultrasound practice
19546330.patient_population: 126 pregnant women in the second trimester (107 successful cardiac volume acquisitions)
19546330.model_description: SonoVCAD, a commercial sonography-based volume computer-aided diagnosis software (GE Healthcare), automatically extracts standard diagnostic fetal cardiac planes (4-chamber view, left and right ventricular outflow tracts, stomach) from a single acquired 3D cardiac ultrasound volume.
19546330.release_evidence: Sonography-Based Volume Computer-Aided Diagnosis software (SonoVCAD; GE Healthcare, Milwaukee, WI)
19546330.headline_result: extended basic fetal cardiac examination achievable in 46.6% of cases; diagnostic planes visible in 62.1%-92.2% of cases depending on plane
19546330.study_design: prospective feasibility study in routine clinical ultrasound practice

20033591.body_region: abdomen and thorax (spine, diaphragm, pelvis, to assist neuroblastoma tumor segmentation)
20033591.clinical_problem: Automatically identifying anatomical landmarks (vertebral column, spinal canal, diaphragm, pelvic girdle) on pediatric CT to assist automatic segmentation of neuroblastoma tumors
20033591.patient_population: 4 pediatric patients with neuroblastoma (10 CT exams)
20033591.model_description: Automated image-processing algorithms identify and segment abdominal and thoracic anatomical landmarks (ribs, vertebral column, spinal canal, diaphragm, pelvic girdle) on pediatric CT images to constrain and assist subsequent automatic segmentation of neuroblastic tumors.
20033591.headline_result: 22.4% average reduction in false-positive tumor segmentation error rate
20033591.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation compared with manual radiologist segmentation

18196306.clinical_problem: Improving the accuracy of estimated fetal weight from ultrasound biometry by detecting and correcting measurement errors in real time
18196306.patient_population: 4075 women in labor (model training/testing); 61 women in the last week of pregnancy (clinical protocol testing)
18196306.model_description: A multinormal probability model, whose parameters are estimated by feed-forward artificial neural networks trained on pregnancy data, checks and corrects real-time ultrasound echobiometric measurements to improve estimated fetal weight accuracy.
18196306.study_design: prospective clinical evaluation of a retrospectively developed neural-network-based probability model

18302119.exclusion_reason: Narrative review of transcranial magnetic stimulation technique and neurophysiology across neurology and psychiatry; no imaging AI component, not pediatric-specific.

16176788.model_family: multivariate texture classifier (gray-level co-occurrence matrix based)
16176788.clinical_problem: Enhancing neonatal cranial ultrasound images to improve visual detection and boundary delineation of periventricular leukomalacia
16176788.model_description: A multivariate texture classifier based on the gray-level co-occurrence matrix, combined with an adaptive texture smoothing filter, enhances the visual contrast between healthy neonatal brain tissue and periventricular leukomalacia-affected tissue to aid computer-aided boundary delineation.
16176788.study_design: retrospective algorithm development compared with manual expert delineation and other speckle filters

41511488.exclusion_reason: Machine learning is used only to estimate environmental exposure levels (air pollution, temperature) from residential addresses; cardiovascular imaging parameters are obtained by standard echocardiography and analyzed with conventional statistics, not AI-based image analysis.

41604954.clinical_problem: Reviewing how deep learning methods are being applied to fetal, infant, and toddler brain imaging research, given the field's especially scarce datasets and high anatomical variability
41604954.patient_population: fetuses, infants and toddlers in neuroimaging research broadly
41604954.model_description: A narrative review, aimed at clinicians and developmental scientists without formal AI training, covering applications of deep learning in fetal, infant, and toddler neuroimaging research, including structural image analysis, enhancement of data acquisition, modeling of cognitive/perceptual processes, and automated video tagging.

41673142.body_region: multiple (radiography, CT, MRI, DEXA, ultrasound across various body regions)
41673142.clinical_problem: Evaluating how much AI models trained on adult imaging data lose performance when applied to pediatric imaging without adaptation, across modalities, tasks and age groups
41673142.patient_population: 16 pediatric imaging dataset cohorts across 20 included studies, ranging from 30 to 7,357 subjects
41673142.model_description: A scoping review of 20 studies evaluating adult-trained AI radiology tools (radiography, CT, MRI, DEXA, ultrasound; segmentation, classification, detection, and mixed tasks) applied to pediatric imaging without retraining, quantifying the resulting performance degradation by modality, task and age group.
41673142.headline_result: pulmonary nodule detection sensitivity dropped from 68-100% (adults) to 26-68% (children); segmentation Dice score reductions >0.10 across organs and modalities; greatest deficits in children 2 years old or younger

42013743.model_name: BIBSNet (Baby and Infant Brain Segmentation Neural Network)
42013743.clinical_problem: Automatically segmenting infant brain tissue on MRI to support studies of typical and atypical early brain development
42013743.model_description: BIBSNet, an open-source deep neural network trained using manually annotated real images plus synthetic segmentations (SynthSeg) with a 10-fold procedure, performs infant brain tissue segmentation that outperforms joint label fusion and is faster at inference, producing FreeSurfer-compatible labels.
42013743.release_evidence: an open-source model for robust and generalizable brain tissue segmentation
42013743.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient: gray matter 0.849 (BIBSNet) vs 0.713 (joint label fusion); white matter 0.862 vs 0.791; BIBSNet is about 600x faster than joint label fusion at inference
42013743.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation against joint label fusion and iBEAT segmentation

39052464.clinical_problem: Automatically and reproducibly measuring cervical length on transvaginal ultrasound to screen for preterm birth risk
39052464.patient_population: pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound cervical length measurement (exact training n not stated)
39052464.model_description: CL-Net, a deep-learning network that incorporates expert anatomical knowledge to identify the cervical canal (a thin, low-contrast structure) on transvaginal ultrasound, automatically and reproducibly measures cervical length to screen for preterm birth risk.
39052464.headline_result: cervical canal recognition success rate 95.5% (CL-Net) vs 96.4% (human experts); median measurement difference from ground truth 1.36 mm (straight cervix), 1.31 mm (curved cervix)
39052464.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation against expert and non-expert measurements

39266284.exclusion_reason: Machine learning is applied to plasma lipidomics data to predict neurofilament light chain levels in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis; MRI lesion counts are used only as a clinical outcome in standard regression analysis, not as AI-analyzed images.

39532533.clinical_problem: Automatically removing facial identifying features from pediatric brain MRI scans (defacing) to enable safe data sharing for pediatric neuroimaging research while preserving research-relevant brain measures
39532533.patient_population: 208 patients with brain tumor (Children's Brain Tumor Network) and 36 clinical control patients (SLIP), ages 7 days to 21 years, 976 total images
39532533.model_description: An nnU-Net-based deep-learning model automatically removes face and ear regions from multiparametric pediatric brain MRI (T1w, T1w-contrast-enhanced, T2w, T2w-FLAIR) to deidentify scans, with minimal downstream impact on brain volume, tumor volume, and temporalis muscle measurements.
39532533.release_evidence: A software package with the trained model is freely provided for wider use and further development (pediatric-auto-defacer; https://github.com/d3b-center/pediatric-auto-defacer-public).
39532533.dataset_size: 976 images from 244 patients (208 brain tumor, 36 clinical control), ages 7 days-21 years
39532533.headline_result: face removal accuracy 98%, ear removal accuracy 73%; downstream brain/tumor volume and temporalis metrics correlated with original images (rS > 0.9, all P < .0001)
39532533.study_design: retrospective model development and validation on a multi-institutional pediatric brain MRI dataset

39793007.model_family: large language / vision-language model (ChatGPT) versus specialized deep-learning classifiers
39793007.clinical_problem: Comparing ChatGPT's ability to detect pneumonia on pediatric chest X-rays against specialized AI models
39793007.model_description: The study compares ChatGPT's performance detecting pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs against specialized AI models trained for that task; no further methodological detail is available because the abstract text was not provided in this record.
39793007.study_design: comparative analysis (abstract text not available in this record)

39818132.model_family: neural network-based methods (attention/saliency, coarse-to-fine, dilated convolution, GANs, spatio-temporal)
39818132.clinical_problem: Reviewing machine-learning methods for automating fetal echocardiography analysis to identify congenital heart defects
39818132.patient_population: review of the fetal echocardiography machine-learning literature (48 papers reviewed in detail)
39818132.model_description: A scoping review of 48 papers on neural-network-based methods for fetal heart anatomy classification and segmentation in fetal echocardiography, covering techniques such as attention/saliency, coarse-to-fine refinement, dilated convolution, generative adversarial networks, and spatio-temporal modeling.

39866856.exclusion_reason: Intraoperative Raman spectroscopy tissue classification for neurosurgical guidance (optical spectroscopy, not radiologic imaging); the model was developed on a primarily adult cohort, with only one pediatric glioblastoma sample used to test generalizability.

39881022.clinical_problem: Generating synthetic sagittal spine radiographs from coronal-view radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis to reduce radiation exposure from biplanar imaging during monitoring
39881022.patient_population: 3,935 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (EOS biplanar radiographic system)
39881022.model_description: A GAN model trained on paired coronal and sagittal EOS radiographs generates synthetic sagittal spine images from coronal views alone; synthetic images were compared with real sagittal radiographs for measurement of lumbar lordosis, sacral slope, pelvic incidence, and sagittal vertical axis.
39881022.headline_result: ICC 0.83-0.88 for synthetic image measurements (vs 0.93-0.99 for real images); correlations between real and synthetic parameters 0.17-0.74; mean absolute errors 7-9 degrees for angular measures and 1.1 cm for sagittal vertical axis; image quality judged insufficient for clinical parameter assessment except for sagittal vertical axis
39881022.study_design: retrospective GAN model development and evaluation against real paired radiographs

39906903.model_family: various machine-learning algorithms (systematic review of 26 studies)
39906903.clinical_problem: Reviewing machine-learning models that predict neurodevelopmental impairment (cognitive, motor, language deficits) in very preterm infants using clinical, neuroimaging, and omics data
39906903.patient_population: very preterm infants (systematic review of 26 studies, January 2018-December 2023)
39906903.model_description: A systematic review of 26 studies applying machine-learning algorithms to clinical and neuroimaging data (and, increasingly, omics data) from very preterm infants to predict later neurodevelopmental impairment.

39931456.model_family: large language model (Gemma-7B) with a distilled BERT-based model
39931456.clinical_problem: Automatically labeling pediatric abdominal X-ray radiology reports for the presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air) of necrotizing enterocolitis, to support NEC research
39931456.patient_population: pediatric abdominal X-ray reports from C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (exact n not stated)
39931456.model_description: AXpert uses a privacy-preserving, instruction-fine-tuned large language model (Gemma-7B) and a distilled BERT-based version to automatically annotate pediatric abdominal X-ray reports for necrotizing enterocolitis presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air), trained and deployed locally.
39931456.headline_result: Gemma-7B F1 score 0.9 ± 0.015 for detecting NEC-positive samples, a 132% improvement over the BlueBERT baseline
39931456.study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation against baseline BERT models

39952550.exclusion_reason: Temporomandibular joint MRI analysis published in a dental journal; TMJ disorder assessment falls within oral/maxillofacial (dental) practice, matching the 'dental' exclusion category rather than general pediatric radiology.

40021764.clinical_problem: Prenatal diagnosis of biliary atresia, a rare and severe congenital disorder that is challenging to detect before birth, from fetal ultrasound
40021764.patient_population: fetuses from 20 hospitals across China and infants from a public database; three independent test cohorts
40021764.model_description: A transfer-learning deep-learning model, pretrained and fine-tuned across multi-institutional fetal ultrasound data, predicts fetal biliary atresia and outperforms both a basic deep-learning model and individual sonologists when used as a diagnostic aid.
40021764.dataset_size: multi-institutional fetal cohort from 20 hospitals plus a public infant database (exact n not stated); three independent test cohorts
40021764.headline_result: AUC 0.906, 0.914, 0.907 across three independent test cohorts (vs 0.793, 0.790, 0.880 for the basic deep-learning model)
40021764.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional model development with independent external test cohorts; registered clinical trial (ChiCTR2200059705)

40024623.clinical_problem: Reviewing the use of artificial intelligence and radiomics in fetal ultrasound imaging
40024623.model_description: A review of the literature on artificial intelligence and radiomics applications in fetal ultrasound, with future perspectives; no further detail is available because the abstract text was not provided in this record.
40024623.study_design: narrative review (abstract text not available in this record)

40036245.clinical_problem: Evaluating whether functional connectivity of dopamine-related brain regions on fMRI can serve as a diagnostic biomarker and subtyping tool for autism spectrum disorder in children
40036245.patient_population: 551 children from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) database
40036245.model_description: Functional connectivity between dopamine-related regions of interest and across the whole brain, derived from resting-state fMRI, is analyzed with machine-learning clustering methods to predict autism spectrum disorder and identify functional-connectivity-based subtypes.
40036245.study_design: retrospective case-control study using a public multi-site neuroimaging database

40038733.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring coronal and sagittal spinal alignment parameters (Cobb angle and sagittal parameters) on biplanar radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
40038733.model_description: A deep-learning model using a ResNet34 backbone performs keypoint detection to automatically measure the coronal Cobb angle and sagittal spinal alignment parameters on biplanar radiographs, compared against manual measurement by two senior spinal surgeons.
40038733.headline_result: mean absolute difference 2.15 degrees (coronal), 2.72 degrees (sagittal); ICC 0.985/0.927; diagnostic accuracy 97.2%, AUC 0.972
40038733.study_design: retrospective model development with internal train/test split, compared against manual surgeon measurements

40045095.exclusion_reason: General-purpose 3D medical image segmentation framework demonstrated across six clinical applications (orthopedics, orbit, mandible CT, cardiac CT, fetal MRI, lung CT); not focused on pediatric or fetal imaging specifically, and no pediatric-specific results are reported separately.

40066351.model_family: deep learning models (various, reviewed across 9 studies)
40066351.clinical_problem: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-powered ultrasound for detecting congenital heart disease in second-trimester fetuses during prenatal cardiac screening
40066351.patient_population: 9 studies included in the meta-analysis (from 374 screened)
40066351.model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 studies evaluating deep-learning models applied to fetal ultrasound or echocardiographic images for detecting congenital heart disease during second-trimester prenatal screening.

40073667.exclusion_reason: Uses functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), an optical neuroimaging technique outside standard radiologic modalities, with conventional graph-theoretical statistical analysis rather than a machine-learning model.

40073783.exclusion_reason: Adult population study predicting skeletal fluorosis risk from demographic and clinical survey variables (age, education, height, MMSE score); children are used only to select study areas via dental fluorosis detection rates, not as the study population, and the model does not use image features as input.

40096208.exclusion_reason: Review of non-invasive fetal electrocardiography (ECG) signal monitoring technology; not radiologic imaging.

40109992.exclusion_reason: Editorial on neuroimaging and machine learning for major depressive disorder diagnosis broadly, not pediatric-specific; adolescents are mentioned only in passing regarding diagnostic challenges.

40115915.exclusion_reason: Adult population with hepatocellular carcinoma and portal hypertension; not pediatric.

40128812.clinical_problem: Validating and implementing an AI-based ultrasound tool for gestational age estimation as part of a broader pre-eclampsia risk-screening and prevention program in resource-limited settings
40128812.patient_population: pregnant women in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa (formative qualitative/quantitative study)
40128812.model_description: As part of the formative phase of the PEARLS trial, an artificial-intelligence ultrasound tool for estimating gestational age will be validated and implemented alongside a pre-eclampsia risk-screening algorithm; this protocol paper describes qualitative and quantitative feasibility research (interviews, focus groups, surveys) rather than the AI tool's technical performance.
40128812.study_design: mixed-methods formative research study protocol (trial registration PACTR202403785563823)

40186143.model_family: LASSO regression / radiomics-based logistic regression models
40186143.clinical_problem: Predicting placenta accreta spectrum and high postpartum hemorrhage risk before delivery from T2-weighted MRI radiomics
40186143.patient_population: 433 women with singleton pregnancies (208 PAS, 225 non-PAS; 80 PPH-positive, 353 PPH-negative)
40186143.model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted MRI are selected via Pearson correlation and LASSO regression and combined with clinical risk factors in nomogram-based clinical-radiomics models predicting placenta accreta spectrum and postpartum hemorrhage risk.
40186143.headline_result: clinical-radiomics model AUC 0.918 (training)/0.885 (test) for PAS; AUC 0.918 (training)/0.905 (test) for PPH
40186143.study_design: retrospective single-institution model development with internal train/test split

40210002.model_family: support vector machine (best of random forest, logistic regression, SVM)
40210002.clinical_problem: Predicting impaired differential renal function (below 40%) in children with unilateral hydronephrosis from urinary tract ultrasound parameters, to guide surgical decision-making without requiring a renogram
40210002.model_description: Machine-learning models (random forest, logistic regression, support vector machine) use urinary tract ultrasound parameters, including renal pelvis diameter, calyx dilation and renal length ratio, plus patient age, to predict differential renal function below 40% in children with unilateral hydronephrosis.

40227327.clinical_problem: Evaluating whether an AI-based training module using an automated fracture-detection tool improves resident and medical student accuracy in detecting pediatric fractures on radiographs
40227327.patient_population: 240 pediatric upper-extremity radiographic examinations reviewed by 4 medical students and 4 PGY-2 radiology residents
40227327.model_description: A previously developed open-source deep-learning fracture-detection algorithm (childfx.com) automatically annotates pediatric upper-extremity radiographs for fractures; trainees reviewed these AI annotations as a teaching tool, and pre/post-training fracture-detection accuracy was compared.
40227327.release_evidence: A previously developed open-source deep learning fracture detection algorithm (www.childfx.com) was used to annotate radiographs.
40227327.headline_result: resident fracture-detection accuracy improved from 71.3% to 77.5% (p=0.032) after AI-based training; medical student accuracy unchanged (56.3% to 57.3%, p=0.794)
40227327.study_design: prospective educational intervention study with pre/post comparison

40234697.clinical_problem: Predicting pediatric bone mineral density (and classifying low-BMD/osteoporosis risk) from plain spine radiographs, as an alternative to DXA
40234697.patient_population: 601 patients aged 10-20 years who underwent DXA and radiography within 6 months
40234697.model_description: A two-stage deep-learning model first uses YOLOv8 to detect vertebral bodies on plain spine radiographs, then a ResNet-18-based regression model predicts bone mineral density values, from which patients are classified into low-BMD versus normal groups based on Z-scores.
40234697.headline_result: vertebral detection AP50 0.97; BMD prediction correlation r=0.72, ICC 0.64; low-BMD classification AUC 0.85, sensitivity 0.76, specificity 0.87
40234697.study_design: retrospective model development and validation against DXA reference standard

40265361.model_family: automated segmentation pipelines (FSL, FreeSurfer, volBrain, SPM12, SimNIBS)
40265361.clinical_problem: Evaluating the accuracy of automated brain MRI segmentation pipelines, developed on neurotypical atlases, for tracking neurodegeneration in children with GM1 gangliosidosis compared to manual segmentation
40265361.patient_population: 16 juvenile and 8 late-infantile GM1 gangliosidosis patients (56 MRI scans) and 11 neurotypical controls (19 MRI scans)
40265361.model_description: Five existing fully automated brain MRI segmentation pipelines (FSL, FreeSurfer, volBrain, SPM12, SimNIBS) are compared against manual segmentation for measuring brain structure volumes (whole brain, thalamus, ventricles, caudate, lentiform nucleus, corpus callosum, cerebellum) in children with GM1 gangliosidosis and neurotypical controls.
40265361.release_evidence: compared five fully automated segmentation pipelines, including FSL, Freesurfer, volBrain, SPM12, and SimNIBS (established freely available academic neuroimaging tools)
40265361.dataset_size: 45 MRI scans (16 juvenile patients), 11 MRI scans (8 late-infantile patients), 19 MRI scans (11 neurotypical controls)
40265361.headline_result: volBrain's vol2Brain pipeline had the strongest correlation with manual segmentation for whole brain, ventricles, and thalamus; FreeSurfer's recon-all strongest for the caudate nucleus
40265361.study_design: retrospective comparison of automated segmentation pipelines against manual segmentation

40268244.clinical_problem: Predicting general psychopathology risk, including major depressive disorder, in adolescents from resting-state functional MRI connectivity, and testing whether a model trained on US adolescents generalizes to Korean adolescents
40268244.patient_population: 6,905 ABCD Study adolescents (US) for pretraining; 125 adolescents (healthy and with major depressive disorder) from Seoul National University Hospital for transfer
40268244.model_description: A deep neural network trained to predict a general psychopathology factor from resting-state functional connectivity MRI in a large US adolescent cohort (ABCD Study) is transferred and fine-tuned to predict psychopathology scores in an independent Korean adolescent cohort, compared against kernel ridge regression and a baseline DNN.
40268244.headline_result: transferred DNN Pearson r=0.29±0.18, mean absolute error 0.59±0.09 (p<.005), outperforming kernel ridge regression and a baseline DNN
40268244.study_design: retrospective model development with external transfer-learning validation across independent multi-site cohorts

40282852.clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI-enhanced echocardiography can improve detection of congenital heart defects in the fetus, including image quality control, cardiac function measurement, defect detection and classification
40282852.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal echocardiography (review, no specific cohort)
40282852.model_description: A mini-review of AI applications in fetal echocardiography, covering image quality control, cardiac function measurement, and defect detection/classification, noting AI-based congenital heart defect detection sensitivity above 90% as a potential prenatal screening tool, particularly for low-resource settings via tele-echocardiography.
40282852.headline_result: AI-based congenital heart defect detection sensitivity greater than 90% in the fetus, as reported across the reviewed literature

40313675.model_family: CNNs, SVMs, and deep-learning methods (including Oct-U-Net and PAICS)
40313675.clinical_problem: Reviewing how AI and machine learning improve early detection, prediction, and assessment of neural tube defects through prenatal ultrasound
40313675.patient_population: review of studies using fetal ultrasound images, genetic data, and maternal health records for neural tube defect detection
40313675.model_description: A review of AI and machine-learning techniques (CNNs, SVMs, and deep-learning segmentation/detection methods such as Oct-U-Net and PAICS) applied to prenatal ultrasound, genetic data, and maternal health records for detecting and predicting neural tube defects.
40313675.headline_result: detection accuracy up to 95%; AI-assisted ultrasound sensitivity 88.9% and specificity 98.0% (versus 81.5%/92.2% for traditional methods); deep-learning models (Oct-U-Net, PAICS) recall/precision 0.93/0.96

40339967.exclusion_reason: Predicts neonatal birth weight from tabular maternal clinical, nutritional, and lifestyle data using a TabNet deep-learning model; the abstract explicitly contrasts this with traditional ultrasonography-based prediction and does not use imaging inputs.

40343188.model_family: CNN and transformer models (six networks compared; DenseNet201 with transfer learning best)
40343188.clinical_problem: Classifying osteopenia versus healthy bone from pediatric wrist X-rays as an alternative to bone mineral density assessment, with interpretable visual explanations
40343188.patient_population: pediatric wrist X-rays from the GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset
40343188.model_description: Six deep networks (CNNs and transformer models) are trained to classify osteopenia versus healthy bone from pediatric wrist X-rays in the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, with two explainable-AI techniques used to visualize and interpret the networks' decisions.
40343188.dataset_size: GRAZPEDWRI-DX pediatric wrist X-ray dataset (exact n not stated)
40343188.headline_result: DenseNet201 with transfer learning achieved the top classification accuracy of 95.2%
40343188.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and evaluation on a public pediatric wrist radiograph dataset

40344610.exclusion_reason: Narrative review of pulmonary MRI technique and clinical applications across all patient populations; AI is mentioned only briefly as a future development direction, not the review's focus, and pediatric patients are mentioned only as one beneficiary group among several (pregnant women, patients needing longitudinal monitoring).

40402200.model_family: radiomics with machine learning (Stochastic Gradient Descent classifier)
40402200.clinical_problem: Predicting whether pediatric low-grade glioma patients have tumor-related epilepsy, non-invasively, from preoperative MRI, to guide preoperative and surgical planning
40402200.patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (exact n not stated)
40402200.model_description: A radiomics-based framework integrates tumor and peritumoral features extracted from preoperative multiparametric MRI, using a Stochastic Gradient Descent classifier, to non-invasively predict tumor-related epilepsy in pediatric low-grade glioma patients.

40408875.model_name: FastSurfer and QuickNAT (existing whole-brain segmentation tools evaluated)
40408875.clinical_problem: Evaluating the accuracy of automated whole-brain segmentation tools for measuring lateral ventricle volume in children with hydrocephalus, compared to manual segmentation
40408875.patient_population: 40 scans from 32 pediatric patients (age 0-18 years) with hydrocephalus
40408875.model_description: Two existing deep-learning whole-brain segmentation tools, FastSurfer and QuickNAT, are applied to automatically segment the lateral ventricles on MRI in children with hydrocephalus, and their accuracy is compared against manual segmentation using the Dice similarity coefficient.
40408875.release_evidence: Two popular, fast, whole-brain segmentation tools were used (FastSurfer and QuickNAT), both established open-source academic segmentation tools.
40408875.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.61 for both FastSurfer and QuickNAT; younger age and larger ventricular volume significantly associated with lower Dice scores
40408875.study_design: retrospective evaluation of existing automated segmentation tools against manual segmentation

40410653.exclusion_reason: Systematic review of deep-learning spinopelvic parameter measurement explicitly restricted to adult spinal deformity; pediatric-focused studies were an exclusion criterion of this review.
